content:
ops-bot: alert: apiserver 5xx spike in eu-west1; severity P2 :rotating_light:
sam: seeing 50-80% 5xx on the apiserver LB for the last 8m, controllers flapping
lina: controller-manager logs show repeated "failed to acquire lease" + frequent restarts (~20-40s)
ez: etcd: wal fsync spikes to 60ms and short i/o timeouts around same window
maya: GPU provisioner reports ~120 attach failures in 10m in eu-west1, node attach backlog growing -> autoscaler keeps retrying
sam: that will churn watch events and increase watch fanout load to apiserver
oz: checked NAT gateways: conntrack usage at 92% on eu-west1 NATs, TIME_WAIT high on apiserver hosts :warning:
eric: ephemeral port exhaustion can surface as 502/503 from the proxy, matches symptoms
maya: mitigation proposal: throttle provisioner retry policy + leader election jitter for provisioner + bump conntrack on NATs temporarily
sam: please grep controller-manager: kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/controller-manager --since=15m | grep -i "failed to acquire lease"
oz: running now, output shows ~300 lease failures between 2025-10-12T01:20 and 01:28 clustered with apiserver 503s
ops-bot: uptime-check: apiserver frontends report connection reset bursts and high TIME_WAIT counts
eric: tail of etcd logs: "WAL sync took 58ms" entries with matching timestamps; disk iops jitter on the NVMe pool reported by cloud provider
lina: can we reduce watch pressure quickly? maybe flip provisioner to exponential backoff (now linear 5s->10s) to 5s->90s
maya: deploy canary backoff change now to 5s->90s for attach retries in eu-west1 provisioner set
sam: also add iptables rate-limit for provisioner pods to avoid retry floods: example rule applied on node pool

```
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -m connlimit --connlimit-above 50 -j DROP
```

oz: bumped conntrack.max on NAT nodes from 65536 -> 200000 as temporary relief
eric: modified kube-apiserver flags on the LB to lower max-requests-inflight for non-critical endpoints to ease tail latency
maya: routing change: moved non-urgent batch GPUs to us-east region to reduce attach pressure in eu-west (temporary)
lina: restarted controller-manager replicas sequentially with 45s graceful drain to let leader settle
sam: still seeing some etcd wal spikes; looks like underlying volume jitter. recommend migrating etcd onto dedicated NVMe pool with higher IOPS
finance-bot: cost estimate request received: NVMe dedicated pool in eu-west1 delta ~$1.8k/month for cluster, plus one-time migration labor
sam: thanks. short term plan: 1) provisioner backoff canary 2) conntrack bump 3) iptables rate-limit 4) route batch to us-east 5) monitor for 30-60m -> if not stable, schedule NVMe migration during maintenance window
eric: created temporary Grafana dashboard: alerts for conntrack>85%, apiserver_5xx_rate>0.04, etcd_wal_fsync_ms>25ms
maya: opened ticket INF-2345 for NVMe migration with perf benchmarks and rollback steps, ETA EOD
oz: post-incident task: consider reserved capacity / pod placement policies to avoid autoscaler storms during region pressure
lina: also propose changing provisioner to hold a small attach token bucket to slow parallel attach attempts
sam: updating runbook with steps + rollback and adding incident notes: runbook-ref: apiserver-conntrack-attach-v1 :memo:
ops-bot: incident note appended to tracker INF-2025-10-12-1
eric: marking the ops thread as active, will post updates in 10m :white_check_mark:
